criteria.reasoning: The report says "He co-founded Netflix in 1998," which is a Netflix founding year other than 1997. The criterion fails any founding year other than 1997, so this fails even though the January 2023 CEO transition is correct.

The only Netflix role reference is historical: "serving as CEO for 25 years until transitioning to Executive Chairman in January 2023." The "Current Board Roles" list names only Bloomberg and [the assistant], with no Facebook/Meta or Microsoft seat. Nothing states in the present tense that he is CEO or Executive Chairman today.
The report never mentions his April 2026 announcement that he will not stand for re-election to Netflix's board at the June 2026 annual meeting.

The report states "His wealth is largely tied to Netflix stock" and gives net worth "between $5.1 billion and $6.6 billion ... [Forbes, 2026; Wikipedia, May 2025 estimate]." The whole range is within $3–8 billion and is sourced and dated, and the report claims no 2%+ stake.
Patty Quillin is never named anywhere in the report. The HBCU gift and the Giving Pledge are attributed to Hastings alone.

The report says he "utilizes a donor-advised fund (DAF) at the Silicon Valley Community Foundation, which he originally opened in 2016 with a $100 million contribution." It also says he "Launched the Hastings Fund dedicated to children's education" with a "$100 Million Pledge (2016)." Together these describe a $100M 2016 education fund held as a DAF at SVCF, and the report never calls it a private foundation.

The report states "In 2024, he gifted two million Netflix shares, valued at $1.1 billion, to his donor-advised fund" and "$1.1 Billion (2024): Transferred in Netflix shares to his donor-advised fund at the Silicon Valley Community Foundation." The share count, value, year and recipient all match.

The City Fund appears only as a board seat ("He is also on the boards of the KIPP Foundation and The City Fund"). The report does not identify it as a channel of his charter philanthropy, give its 2018 launch, name the Arnolds as anchor partners or give the ~$200 million raised.

The report lists "$120 Million (2020): Donated to support scholarships at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), split equally among the United Negro College Fund, Morehouse College, and Spelman College." That gives the correct total, year and three recipients, and the equal split implies $40 million each. Leaving out Quillin is not among this criterion's fail conditions; C-005 tests it.

The report says "Hastings sits on the board of the **Charter School Growth Fund (CSGF)**, which specifically lists an office in **Denver, Colorado**." It places CSGF in Colorado, describes the seat as current, and does not say he chairs it.
The report never mentions Lone Rock, the educators' retreat in Bailey, Colorado, or the Lone Rock Foundation.
The report estimates he "has the capacity to make a **$10 million to $50 million+ transformational gift** to an education nonprofit." The top of that range is above $40 million.

The report routes the approach through his charter network: CSGF is "your warmest and most direct path of introduction," and "Leveraging leaders within" KIPP and The City Fund gives secondary introduction routes. It does not recommend a cold letter, an unsolicited proposal or contact through Netflix.
The report says "He co-founded Netflix in 1998," which contradicts fact sheet row 1.1 (co-founded in 1997). The tolerances allow 1998 only for the launch of the DVD service, not for the co-founding.
